method: Minutes come from the NBA model: a three-season history prior, this season's box scores weighted toward recent games, a pull toward starter minutes once a player starts, and a team fit to 240 minutes in which an OUT player's minutes are shared across everyone left. Each stat is minutes times a per-minute rate (history, recent form, pace, opponent, usage and on/off splits with teammates out). The depth chart then blends the model with each player's last-10 average, by role, with weights chosen on October to January and tested on February to April 2026; players back from a 3+ game absence use the model alone on most stats. Minutes are minutes if he plays, so a team's chart can add up past 240 (deep benches rarely all play; forcing 240 made the backtest worse, 5.01 to 5.22 minutes MAE). Starter means the team's five highest projected minutes (the confirmed five once posted), Rotation 12+ projected minutes, Bench the rest, Out on the injury report.
